statement: A J event reaches a hosted Entity in the chain's order (block, then log index) and, across batches and a repeat from the old cursor, once in effect: a block that is missing, out of order or on another fork refuses the delivery and the cursor does not move.
source: consolidation-plan.md D9 and J2 (events applied once and in order); R-HTLC-CLOCK (the delivered height is the Host's finalizedJHeight)

layers.arrival: n/a: the watcher is Host code that reads a node; the Arrival specs take J events as given
layers.quint: owed: spec thread (spec/quint/runtime.qnt part 3 `exactly_once_j` and its mutants in spec/quint/mutants/runtime.json, QUESTIONS R2, are the spec side; no name carries this id yet)
layers.contract: n/a: no contract code takes part; the watcher reads the deployed Depository's events
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-WATCH-ORDER a log that names a block of the batch by its hash but claims another number is refused
R-WATCH-ORDER one delivery is the chain's events for each hosted Entity in order, to its last block
R-WATCH-ORDER an Entity that is not hosted is told nothing, and the delivery still moves the cursor
R-WATCH-ORDER a block that does not follow the one before it is a broken chain, a missing one is a gap
R-WATCH-ORDER a log of a block the batch does not hold, or of another fork's block, is refused
R-WATCH-ORDER logs that run backwards or repeat are refused, not sorted or deduplicated
R-WATCH-ORDER however the blocks are cut into batches, the events are the chain's, once each, in order
R-WATCH-ORDER a delivery repeated from the old cursor, as after a crash, is the same delivery
